title: GPS Speedometer Online: Live Speed in Browser
description: Read an approximate device speed, session distance and elapsed time in your browser. Not a certified speedometer.
summary_sentence: Location fixes and calculated trip statistics are processed for the current session; readings may be inaccurate.
quick_answer: With permission, the tool uses browser geolocation and displays device speed when available, or an estimate from successive positions. Distance and speed can be affected by inaccurate fixes. Do not rely on it for driving or safety-critical decisions.
steps_intro: Your phone already knows your speed. Let the browser show it:

body.t: Speed readings are not certified and can be noisy. Passengers may compare readings cautiously; a driver should not operate this tool while driving.
Anything that moves without a dial gets one: sailing speed, a borrowed bike, the train window argument about how fast 'this thing' goes.
The navigator's speed readout, hands-free from the driver's dial — and the distance counter for 'how far since the services'.
A speed that flickers at a standstill is your fix quality confessing. Open sky settles it; tunnels erase it — see the FAQs.
At rest, a good fix reads 0 with an occasional flicker; a poor fix wanders through small speeds as the position jitters. The flicker is the accuracy of your phone, demonstrated live.
The page remembers the session's peak speed and accumulates distance while it runs — a pocket trip computer for the length of the journey.

faq: How accurate is it?
Accuracy varies with device, signal and movement. Speed can be missing or noisy, particularly indoors or near obstructions; the tool is not certified.
Does it work on a laptop?
If the laptop's browser can get a position (Wi-Fi positioning), a coarse version works; phones and tablets with GPS are the real instrument.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
The speedometer is your location in motion — it needs the permission, and declining it simply means no stream. Nothing is uploaded or stored either way.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Unrelated to speed, but the same data family: maps and records vary by source. Your speed is computed from satellites, not maps.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No — the stream is processed on the device for this page's display.
Why does it flicker at a standstill?
Position jitter: each fix wobbles by metres, and speed computed from wobbling positions invents small motion. A 'deadband' in your head fixes it.
mph or km/h?
Both are shown — the pair is the point for travellers crossing the channel of units.
Does it record my trip?
It accumulates distance and peak while the page runs; close the page and the session is gone. Recording for keeps is a tracker app's job, not this page's.
Battery drain?
GPS is hungry. For long journeys, a charger is the speedometer's best friend.
Can I use it while driving?
Do not operate this page while driving. It is not a certified speedometer; follow local laws and use the vehicle instrument.
Altitude shown?
The speedometer's job is speed, peak and distance. Elevation has a dedicated finder on this site for the vertical number.
